title: RAY Robotics
summary: Co-founding an autonomous last-mile delivery robot as my Berkeley MEng capstone — leading a team of 10.
description: RAY is my UC Berkeley MEng capstone: an autonomous last-mile delivery system built by a team of 10. I run our rapid-prototyping cycles and design reviews, hold us to a bar of engineering excellence, and lead funding and customer-discovery efforts alongside the build.

title: NOVA Robotics & AI Community
summary: First non-founder member of NOVA, building a robotics & AI community across academia, industry, and policy.
description: NOVA — the Network for Open Vision & Advancement in robotics & AI — is a community I help run as its first non-founder member. I coordinate conferences, roundtables, and outreach, connecting academics, professionals, and policy figures across UC Berkeley and MIT to talk about where robotics and AI are headed.

title: Neptune — Underwater Comms
summary: Led final integration of Neptune, a wireless underwater comms system for scuba divers, across an 18-person team.
description: For MIT's 2.009 product engineering course I helped build Neptune, a wireless underwater communication system for divers. I worked on mechanical design, waterproofing, and PCB design, drove customer discovery, presented at the mid-semester Architecture Review, and led final integration of the 18-person team.

title: Pneumatic Soft Gripper
summary: Designed and built a pneumatic soft gripper from scratch — custom inflatable actuators, 3D-printed parts, and a force-sensing control loop.
description: In Berkeley's ME 292C (Design with Morphing Materials & Mechanisms) I built a pneumatic robotic gripper end to end: custom inflatable actuators cast from EcoFlex and silicone, 3D-printed structure, and a control system driven by force-sensitive resistors. I owned the system architecture and iterated the materials to get a reliable grip.

title: Wearable Sit-to-Stand Device
summary: Built a wearable sit-to-stand assistive device with Micropython/C++ control.
description: For Berkeley's ME 239 (Robotic Locomotion) I designed a wearable sit-to-stand assistive device and wrote its control code in Micropython and C++. I shaped the system architecture, built the protoboard and sensing, and led final integration to a working demo.

title: Toyota Racing Development
summary: Vehicle systems intern: thermal modeling, custom motor-control PCBs, and a precision encoder-wheel test rig for GR Corolla race cars.
description: As a vehicle systems engineering intern at Toyota Racing Development I wrote thermal-modeling code, designed custom PCBs for motor control and power management, and built a benchtop encoder-wheel test rig to 1mm tolerance — production-level work preparing GR Corolla race cars.

title: Bio-Inspired Swinging Robot
summary: Built and optimized an underactuated swinging robot, benchmarked against human motion.
description: In MIT's 2.74 (Bio-Inspired Robotics) I built an underactuated swinging robot and optimized it for swing height and joint efficiency, comparing its motion to human mechanics. I made the final poster and presented the work live.

title: Feedback Control Systems
summary: Characterized dynamic systems and implemented digital controllers — root locus, Bode, Nyquist, and quantization effects.
description: MIT's 2.14 (Analysis & Design of Feedback Control Systems): I characterized a range of systems and wrote up the analysis, hand-sketching then measuring and simulating root locus, Bode, and Nyquist plots, and investigating quantization effects in digital controller implementations.

title: MechE Lab Assistant
summary: Lab assistant for MIT's intro robotics and dynamics & controls courses — maintained the robots, ran sections, and graded.
description: For two years I was a lab assistant for MIT MechE's 2.12 (Intro to Robotics) and 2.004 (Dynamics & Control II). I maintained the teaching hardware — MagLev rigs, mobile robots, and self-balancing 'Segway' robots — helped shape project parameters, ran lab sections, and graded.

title: Archerfish Lab Automation
summary: Co-author: retrofitted a 3D printer into a high-throughput lab-automation platform for solar-materials discovery.
description: At MIT's Accelerated Materials Lab for Sustainability I built hardware and software to automate lab testing, turning a 3D printer into a continuous, hands-off experimentation platform for perovskite solar-cell precursor discovery. The work became the paper 'Archerfish: a retrofitted 3D printer for high-throughput combinatorial experimentation via continuous printing.'

title: Deep Tech Commercialization
summary: Built a commercialization strategy for a Berkeley Lab breakthrough — market research, customer discovery, and an investor pitch.
description: In Berkeley's ENGIN 274 (Deep Tech Commercialization Strategies) my interdisciplinary team took a Berkeley Lab research breakthrough and tested whether it could reach market. I ran market research and customer discovery and presented our findings to investors and policy makers.

title: reFresh — Food Waste Platform
summary: 48-hour sprint: a restaurant-to-nonprofit food-waste platform, from market research to a working mockup.
description: At Berkeley Haas' MBA 292ID Impact Startup sprint I helped create reFresh, a restaurant-to-nonprofit food-waste reduction platform, in 48 hours — running market research and building the technology-platform mockup and pitch.

title: Robotics Affinity Group Lead
summary: Selected to lead events and career outreach for Berkeley's incoming robotics MEng cohort.
description: I was selected to lead the UC Berkeley robotics affinity group, coordinating events and career outreach for the incoming MEng cohort — industry visits, professional speakers, and mixers — and collaborating with NOVA on robotics discussions.
